content: When the body has an excessive number of mast cells, these cells release an abnormally high amount of substances such as histamines. This overproduction can result in symptoms including diarrhea, abdominal pain, itching, skin rash, and flushing. Cromolyn is classified as a mast cell stabilizer, a type of medication designed to prevent the release of these substances. Instructions for Use: Before starting cromolyn, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This should also be reviewed each time you refill the medication. Cromolyn is typically taken orally, as directed by your physician, four times daily—30 minutes before meals and at bedtime. If prescribed for food allergies or inflammatory bowel disease, your doctor may instruct you to take it 15 to 20 minutes before meals. Do not swallow the ampules directly. Instead, the liquid contents of the ampules are used to prepare a solution. Before use, visually inspect the liquid for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the product. To prepare the solution, break open the ampule(s) and squeeze the liquid into a glass of plain water. Do not mix it with fruit juice, soda, milk, or any other fluid. Stir the solution thoroughly and drink it immediately. Do not prepare the solution in advance. This medication does not provide immediate relief. Regular use is necessary to achieve its full benefits, which may take 2 to 3 weeks to become noticeable. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same times each day. This form of cromolyn is intended for oral use only and should not be used for inhalation (e.g., in a nebulizer), nasal application, or injection. Side Effects: Common side effects may include headache, muscle aches, and diarrhea. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to cromolyn are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Precautions: Before taking cromolyn, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, cromolyn should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If you have already eaten, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store the ampules in their foil pouches at room temperature, away from heat and light, until ready for use. Do not store them in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
